title: Delivery reports
no_reports_hint: First reports arrive 1–2 days after the DNS records are in place (see Settings → DNS assistant).
live_hint: New reports are processed as soon as they arrive.
ack_hint: Done issues come back as soon as a new report shows the same problem.
alert_failed_d: Enter an existing mailbox under Settings → Alerts to.
dns_issue_w: Other mail servers send no or only partial reports for these domains.
dns_issue_d: The DNS assistant lists the missing records ready to copy.
unproc_w: They are in the "Unprocessed" folder of {mb} – usually spam or a damaged report.
unproc_d: Have a look and delete them when convenient.
reporter_hint: DMARC: your mail this receiver got. TLS: connections from its servers to your mail server.
causes: Why own mail failed DMARC (90 days)
spoof_hint: Foreign servers that sent in the name of your domains. With p=quarantine/reject receivers put these into spam or reject them.
fwd_hint: Your mail forwarded by someone (e.g. to Gmail). Authentication breaks on the way; the receiver recognised it – usually harmless.
pass_hint: Services allowed to send on your behalf (e.g. newsletter, shop or ticket systems).
mailbox_help: Mailbox that receives the DMARC and TLS reports. Processed reports are deleted from it – use a dedicated mailbox.
alert_help: One or more mailboxes on this server (comma separated), not the report mailbox. Only sent when there is a problem.
ips_help: Mail from these addresses counts as "own". Automatic: like mailcow's DNS check (SNAT_TO_SOURCE or ip4/ip6.mailcow.email).
run_time_help: Server time. Safety net in case a report was not processed right away.
new_mailbox_help: Creates a 200 MB mailbox with a random password (nobody needs to log in) and selects it.
dns_help: For other mail servers to send reports to {mb}, every domain needs these TXT records.
name: Name
dns_all_ok: All domains are fully set up.
mail_subject: ⚠️ Mail server: problem in delivery reports
mail_intro: The automatic analysis of delivery reports (TLS-RPT/DMARC) found problems:
mail_tls: TLS: {org} reports {fail} failed of {total} sessions for {dom}: {details}
mail_dmarc: DMARC: {org} reports {cnt} message(s) from our server ({ip}) for {dom} as FAILED (DKIM {dkim}, SPF {spf})
mail_unreadable: Report "{subject}" from {sender} could not be read ({err}) – moved to {box}/{folder}
mail_summary: Processed: {reports} reports. TLS ok: {tls_ok} sessions. DMARC own server: {ok} ok / {fail} failed.
mail_spoof: FYI – foreign senders spoofing our domains:
mail_kept: Unreadable reports and foreign mail are kept in the folder {folder} of the mailbox {box}.
x_dkim_bad: DKIM signature of {d} (selector {s}) invalid ({r}) – message altered in transit (forwarding, footer, virus scanner) or key does not match DNS
x_dkim_temp: DKIM of {d} could not be checked (temporary DNS error at the receiver)
x_dkim_unaligned: DKIM valid, but signed by {d} instead of {hf} (not aligned)
x_spf_fail: SPF: IP {ip} is not allowed by the SPF record of {d} ({r})
x_spf_temp: SPF of {d} could not be checked (temporary DNS error at the receiver)
x_spf_unaligned: SPF ok for {d}, but not matching the From domain {hf} (not aligned)
x_reason_sampled_out: policy only applied to a sample (pct)
i_dkim_bad_t: {n} of your messages had an invalid signature
i_dkim_bad_w: The digital signature (DKIM) no longer matched. Usually the message was changed in transit – by forwarding, a mailing-list footer or a virus scanner at the receiver.
i_dkim_bad_d: Single cases can be ignored. If it happens often, compare the DKIM key in mailcow (Configuration → ARC/DKIM keys) with the DNS record.
i_dkim_none_t: {n} messages from your server were not signed
i_dkim_none_w: These messages came from your server without a DKIM signature. Usually a device or program (scanner, POS, website) sends directly without logging in.
i_dkim_none_d: Find out which device sent at that time and let it send through a mailbox with SMTP login.
i_unaligned_t: {n} messages were checked for a different domain
i_unaligned_w: Signature or SPF belonged to a different domain than the sender. Typical when an external service (newsletter, shop, booking system) sends on your behalf.
i_unaligned_d: Find the service and set it up for your domain (own DKIM signature or SPF permission).
i_spf_fail_t: {n} messages came from an IP not listed in SPF
i_spf_fail_w: The receiver did not find your sending IP in your SPF record.
i_spf_fail_d: Check the SPF record and add the server IP (the DNS assistant in Settings helps).
i_spf_dns_t: Your SPF record is missing or broken ({n} messages affected)
i_spf_dns_w: Receivers could not evaluate your domain's SPF record.
i_spf_dns_d: Check the SPF record – there must be exactly one, starting with v=spf1.
i_temp_t: {n} messages could not be checked temporarily
i_temp_w: A temporary DNS error at the receiver. This happens now and then.
i_temp_d: Nothing to do as long as it is rare.
i_other_t: {n} of your messages failed the check
i_other_w: The report gives no specific cause.
tlsr_certificate-expired_w: Your mail server's certificate had expired.
tlsr_certificate-expired_d: Renew the certificate in mailcow (normally automatic via Let's Encrypt) and check the ACME logs.
tlsr_certificate-host-mismatch_w: The certificate did not match your mail server's name.
tlsr_certificate-host-mismatch_d: Check that the certificate covers the MX name (mailcow: MAILCOW_HOSTNAME / ADDITIONAL_SAN).
tlsr_certificate-not-trusted_d: Check that the full certificate chain is served.
tlsr_validation-failure_w: The certificate could not be validated.
tlsr_validation-failure_d: Check certificate and chain in mailcow.
tlsr_starttls-not-supported_w: Your server did not offer encryption.
tlsr_starttls-not-supported_d: Check that port 25 reaches mailcow directly and nothing strips STARTTLS.
tlsr_sts-policy-fetch-error_w: The MTA-STS policy could not be fetched.
tlsr_sts-policy-invalid_d: Check the mta-sts.txt contents (mode, mx, max_age).
tlsr_sts-webpki-invalid_w: The MTA-STS web certificate is invalid.
tlsr_tlsa-invalid_w: The DANE/TLSA records don't match the certificate.
tlsr_tlsa-invalid_d: Update TLSA records after every certificate change.
tlsr_dnssec-invalid_d: Check the DNSSEC settings at your DNS provider.
tlsr_other_w: A secure connection to your server failed ({r}).
tlsr_other_d: Check the certificate and port 25 reachability.
i_spoof_w: Foreign servers tried to send in your name. The receivers recognised it.
i_spoof_d: Nothing to do – that's exactly what DMARC is for.
i_fwd_w: Someone forwarded your mail (e.g. to Gmail). Authentication breaks on the way; the receiver recognised it.
language_help: The page itself follows the language selected in mailcow.
run_started: Run started – reload the page in a minute.
